# Using Collections in optree

Ordinary option groups have fixed keys defined in `defaults`. A collection is
useful when the names of records are not all known in advance. It is a named
list, not a data frame: each record has the same required fields and can be
added or updated at runtime.

## Define a collection

Mark the group containing the records with `"_as_collection" = TRUE` in
`defaults`. For each required record field, supply a validator at
`<collection path>._default.<field>`:

```{r}
library(optree)

sources <- create_options_manager(
  defaults = list(
    collection = list(
      folder = "collection",
      items = list(
        "_as_collection" = TRUE,
        code_base = list(type = "files", folder = "code-base", enabled = TRUE),
        crop_model = list(type = "files", folder = "crop-model", enabled = FALSE)
      )
    )
  ),
  validators = list(
    "collection.items._default.type" = v_character_scalar(),
    "collection.items._default.folder" = v_character_scalar(),
    "collection.items._default.enabled" = v_logical_scalar()
  )
)

sources$get("collection.items")
```

The marker is schema metadata, not an item or an option returned by `get()`.
Here `collection.folder` is an ordinary option; the records are under
`collection.items`.

The `_default` validators define the record schema, not default values for
missing fields. Each record must be a named list with **exactly** the declared
fields. Every field is required and unknown fields are rejected. Each
validator receives the complete field value; use a suitable validator for
scalar, vector, or structured values.

Initial records are validated when the manager is created. To start with no
records, supply the marker alone:

```{r}
empty_sources <- create_options_manager(
  defaults = list(items = list("_as_collection" = TRUE)),
  validators = list(
    "items._default.type" = v_character_scalar(),
    "items._default.enabled" = v_logical_scalar()
  )
)
empty_sources$get("items")
```

## Add and update records

Add a record using a new name and supply every declared field:

```{r}
sources$set("collection.items.history" = list(
  type = "commit-history",
  folder = "commit-history",
  enabled = FALSE
))
sources$get("collection.items.history")
```

Update an existing record with only the fields that need to change. You can
use dot-separated paths or nested lists, as with ordinary options:

```{r}
sources$set("collection.items.history.enabled" = TRUE)
sources$set(collection = list(items = list(
  history = list(folder = "history")
)))
sources$get("collection.items.history")
```

In a single `set()` call, changes to the same record are merged before that
record is validated. The complete changed record is checked, but unchanged
records are not revalidated by the `_default` field validators.

```{r}
sources$set(
  "collection.items.history.type" = "history",
  "collection.items.history.enabled" = FALSE
)
```

## Validation and rollback

An incomplete record, an unknown field, or a value rejected by its validator
causes an error. For example:

```{r, error = TRUE}
sources$set("collection.items.new_source" = list(type = "files"))
```

```{r, error = TRUE}
sources$set("collection.items.history.enabled" = "yes")
```

An unsuccessful `set()` leaves all options unchanged, including when a call
tries to update multiple options:

```{r}
before <- sources$get()
tryCatch(
  sources$set(
    "collection.folder" = "new-folder",
    "collection.items.history.extra" = 1
  ),
  error = function(e) message(conditionMessage(e))
)
identical(sources$get(), before)
```

## Collection-wide rules

Use an ordinary validator on the collection path for rules involving the
collection as a whole. It receives the complete collection, and, like other
ordinary validators, runs after every `set()` call. Such a validator can inspect
all records, even though `_default` validators only check changed records.
Ordinary validators are not run when the manager is created.

```{r}
limited <- create_options_manager(
  defaults = list(items = list(
    "_as_collection" = TRUE,
    first = list(type = "files")
  )),
  validators = list(
    "items._default.type" = v_character_scalar(),
    items = function(value) {
      if (length(value) > 2) stop("at most two items are allowed")
    }
  )
)
limited$set("items.second" = list(type = "files"))
```

## Names, nesting, and reset

- Record names must be non-empty, unique, and must not contain dots.
- `_default` and `_as_collection` are reserved names within collections.
- A collection may appear at an ordinary option path, including the root, but
  collections cannot be nested inside collection records.
- `_default` validators describe direct record fields; validators for
  individual records or nested field paths are not supported.
- Each collection must declare at least one `_default` field validator.

`reset()` restores the original defaults, including the original records and
their values. Records added later are removed:

```{r}
sources$reset()
names(sources$get("collection.items"))
sources$get("collection.items.crop_model.enabled")
```
